handoff: ACs met and traced; blocking F1: an untracked .gitattributes makes upgrade exit 1 (git add on a deleted file) or stage a file the person never added (upgrade.ts:205). Minor F2-F4, nits F5-F6.

findings.title: An untracked .gitattributes crashes upgrade or gets staged
findings.detail:
runStatePart calls ctx.git.stage(root, ['.gitattributes']) whenever dropRunsAttribute changed the file, without checking whether git tracks it. Repro in a harness repo after init, commit and push: write an untracked .gitattributes that holds only the two S10 lines, then run `norn upgrade --json`. dropRunsAttribute (old-layout.ts:74) deletes the file and git add fails, so upgrade exits 1 with `git add failed (exit 128): fatal: pathspec '.gitattributes' did not match any files`. This happens after the refs were pushed and the git rm was staged, so the report is lost. With an untracked file that also holds the person's own lines ('*.png binary'), upgrade exits 0 and stages .gitattributes, a file the person never added. That contradicts upgrade's own rule for untracked files (moveLayout: 'Untracked before, so not staged'; LY3 stages only norn's moves).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Stage .gitattributes only when it is tracked (git ls-files), or else report it as untracked and not staged, the way moveLayout does. Add a test for an untracked file.

findings.title: Without a resolvable remote the record goes to a local ref only, but upgrade reports 'pushed' and stages the removal
findings.detail:
gitRemote returns null when git_remote names no remote. casRefs then only writes local refs, and the removal is still staged. GR6c says the record is pushed before the removal is staged, and the markdown (upgrade.ts:263) says 'pushed'. The run state stays in git history, so nothing is lost, but the output overstates what happened.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Name the local-only case in the outcome or the markdown, or keep the removal unstaged when there is no remote.

findings.title: Safety paths without a test
findings.detail:
No test covers: an unreadable remote (commit 7ad7c538c; checked by hand: every story failed, nothing staged, no refs); a remote ref that holds another record (checked by hand: failed, nothing staged); no remote; dropRunsAttribute deleting a file left empty; and a rerun after the removal is staged (the ls-files index check). AC3 asserts that the push failed, but not the remote's own reason ('archive refused').
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add at least the unreadable-remote and another-record cases at seam S1.

findings.title: The .gitattributes line is dropped and RUN_STATE_COMMIT suggested even when no run state moved
findings.detail:
With an unreadable remote every story fails, but the S10 line is still dropped and staged. The commit offered is then 'Move norn run state to archive refs' although no run state moved.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Pick the commit message from what actually moved.

findings.title: The reason says 'its record fails validation' when commit-tree failed or the path is missing
findings.detail:
treeRecordCommit returns the commit-tree failure as errors, and the caller labels every error as a validation failure. A multi-line git stderr in the reason also breaks the markdown bullet.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Tell the two failures apart, and keep the reason to one line in the markdown.

findings.title: Duplicated Code / Long Function in archiveBaseRunState
findings.detail:
The outcome literal is built at five sites, and treeStoryRunStatePath and recordRef are recomputed in three loops. The function discovers the stories, reads the remote, packs, pushes, retries and removes in one body of about 60 lines. The import order at upgrade.ts:38 is also off (machineHolder before dropOldIgnoreLine).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Add an outcome(s, done, extra) helper and split discovery from push and remove.
